observations.title: Análisis de mejoras — Sharewell Baby
observations.content:
**What**: Análisis completo de oportunidades de mejora para Sharewell Baby (app de gastos compartidos)
**Why**: El usuario pidió analizar el proyecto y generar oportunidades de mejora
**Where**: agents/oportunidades-de-mejora.md (22 puntos identificados)
**Learned**: 
- El proyecto no tiene tests, es crítico para una app financiera
- La página de reportes tiene un double-fetch bug que duplica todas las queries
- `useMemo` usado con side effects en 3 lugares (anti-patrón React)
- `confirm()` bloqueante para operaciones destructivas
- No hay staleTime configurado en TanStack Query
- CATEGORIES array duplicado en 2 route files
- Route files muy grandes (640 y 324 líneas) con dialog components co-locados

observations.title: Refactored expense form with zod + react-hook-form + autosave

observations.title: Explored recurring expenses + UTM architecture
observations.content:
**What**: Explored architecture for UTM (Chilean inflation-adjusted tax unit) and recurring expenses features.
**Why**: Parents need to track school expenses defined in UTM but paid in CLP, and create recurring monthly expenses from templates.
**Where**: `src/routes/app.gastos.nuevo.tsx`, `src/routes/app.gastos.$expenseId.tsx`, `src/lib/finance.ts`, `src/hooks/use-queries.ts`, `supabase/migrations/`
**Learned**: 
- UTM values should live in a `utm_values` Supabase table seeded manually yearly. Convert UTM→CLP at creation time (using expense month's UTM value), store `total_amount` in CLP. No changes to finance engine.
- Recurring expenses should use a `recurring_expenses` template table with manual "generate" button (no cron, no pg_cron available). Add `recurring_source_id` FK to expenses for tracking.
- Schema needs: `utm_values` table, `recurring_expenses` + `recurring_expense_shares` tables, 4 new columns on `expenses` (is_utm, utm_amount, utm_value_at_expense, recurring_source_id).
- Key risk mitigation: check for existing expense before generating recurring (avoid duplicates), store UTM value at conversion time (no retroactive changes to old expenses).

observations.title: Session summary: sharewell-baby
observations.content:
## Goal
Implement change "fase7-utm-recurrentes" — add UTM value storage, recurring expense templates, and UTM→CLP conversion to the Sharewell Baby expense tracking app.

## Instructions
- Files are tracked with both staged and unstaged changes — staged changes include hooks barrel export, use-queries type update, types.ts, use-recurring.ts, and utm.ts
- Use `as any` with eslint-disable comments for supabase table inserts on new tables that haven't been covered by auto-generated types yet
- Manually added new table types (utm_values, recurring_expenses) and new expense columns (utm_amount, recurring_source_id) to src/integrations/supabase/types.ts

## Discoveries
- The supabase auto-generated types (types.ts) don't include new tables until migrations are applied and types are regenerated — must manually add new table shapes for tsc to pass
- `FormLabel` from shadcn requires being inside `FormField` context — crashes if used standalone
- The `ExpenseRow` type in `use-queries.ts` is project-owned and can be updated manually for new columns
- Prettier + ESLint dual config means always run `pnpm format` after edits before linting

## Accomplished
- ✅ Created migration `20260602000001_utm_recurrentes.sql` — utm_values table, recurring_expenses table, ALTER expenses add utm_amount + recurring_source_id columns
- ✅ Created migration `20260602000002_seed_utm_2025.sql` — seeds 12 monthly UTM values for 2025
- ✅ Created `src/lib/utm.ts` — getUtmValueForMonth, utmToClp, formatUtm utilities
- ✅ Created `src/hooks/use-recurring.ts` — useRecurringExpenses, useCreateRecurring, useDeactivateRecurring, useGenerateRecurringExpense hooks
- ✅ Modified `src/routes/app.gastos.nuevo.tsx` — added "Expresado en UTM" toggle switch, UTM amount input, on-submit UTM→CLP conversion
- ✅ Modified `src/routes/app.gastos.$expenseId.tsx` — added UTM badge next to CLP total, recurring source attribution badge
- ✅ Modified `src/routes/app.ninos.$childId.tsx` — added "Gastos recurrentes" section with template list, create dialog, generate/deactivate buttons, status indicators (Generado, Finalizado)
- ✅ Updated `src/hooks/index.ts` — barrel exports for all new hooks + RecurringExpenseRow type
- ✅ Updated `src/hooks/use-queries.ts` — ExpenseRow now includes utm_amount and recurring_source_id
- ✅ Updated `src/lib/forms/expense-schema.ts` — removed `.int()` constraint to allow decimal UTM amounts
- ✅ Updated `src/integrations/supabase/types.ts` — added utm_values, recurring_expenses tables; updated expenses with new columns
- ✅ `pnpm lint` — 0 errors (8 pre-existing warnings only)
- ✅ `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean (no errors)

## Next Steps

observations.title: sdd/explore/offline-support
observations.content:
## Exploration: Offline Support for Sharewell Baby

### Current State

**Service Worker** (`public/sw.js`): 43 lines, network-first for non-Supabase GETs, network-only for Supabase URLs (returns 503 offline). Caches only `/` and `/manifest.webmanifest` on install.

**TanStack Query config** (`src/router.tsx`): `staleTime: 30s`, `gcTime: 5min`. Keeps data in-memory across SPA navigation. Cache is empty on hard refresh.

**Mutations**: `app.gastos.nuevo.tsx` writes directly with `supabase.from(...).insert(...)` — NOT using `useMutation`. Four sequential writes: expense → payment → shares → attachment upload. No offline queue.

**Manifest** (`public/manifest.webmanifest`): `display: "standalone"`, `short_name: "Cuidado"`, SVG icons at 192 and 512. Installable.

### Affected Areas

- `public/sw.js` — rewrite to add stale-while-revalidate for Supabase GETs and mutation queue
- `src/hooks/use-queries.ts` — all 9 query hooks (cold-start caching)
- `src/routes/app.gastos.nuevo.tsx` — offline mutation queue needed (4-step write)
- `src/routes/app.gastos.$expenseId.tsx` — edit/delete mutations
- `src/routes/app.ninos.$childId.tsx` — add-member mutation
- `src/router.tsx` — QueryClient `networkMode` config
- `src/routes/__root.tsx` — SW update handling
- `src/components/app-layout.tsx` — offline banner placement
- `public/manifest.webmanifest` — minor PWA polish

### Approaches

**1. Stale-while-revalidate for Supabase GETs (reads)**
   - SW intercepts Supabase GETs, returns cache immediately, revalidates in background
   - Gap: TQ keeps data in-memory during SPA nav, but hard refresh loses it
   - Pros: Catches cold starts, minimal code change (~20 lines in sw.js), TQ handles freshness
   - Cons: Adds ~20ms to first-load check for cached response
   - Effort: Low

**2. Offline mutation queue (writes)**
   - IndexedDB queue + Background Sync API (`sync` event)
   - Must refactor expense creation from direct `supabase` calls to `useMutation` (currently 4 sequential inserts)
   - Receipt uploads (File/Blob) can't go in IndexedDB easily
   - Conflict resolution is app-specific (duplicate expenses, stale UTM values)
   - Pros: Users can create expenses offline
   - Cons: Major refactor of the expense creation flow, conflict handling, UTM conversion needs network
   - Effort: High

**3. Offline detection + UI**
   - `useOffline()` hook listening to `online`/`offline` events
   - Persistent banner in AppLayout (not a toast)
   - Disable submit buttons with "Sin conexión" tooltip
   - Pros: Cheap, high perceived value, sets foundation for Phase 2
   - Effort: Low

**4. PWA manifest polish**
   - Add `prefer_related_applications: false`, `categories` already present
   - Already installable — icons and display mode are correct
   - Effort: Negligible

### Recommendation

Build in two phases:

**Phase 1 (this change) — reads + awareness:**
1. Stale-while-revalidate for all Supabase GETs in sw.js (catches hard refresh gap)
2. `useOffline()` hook + offline banner in AppLayout
3. Disable submit buttons on mutation forms when offline
4. SW update detection (show "Actualización disponible" prompt)

**Phase 2 (future) — write queue:**
5. Refactor all direct `supabase` writes to `useMutation` hooks
6. IndexedDB queue + Background Sync for expense creation
7. Receipt upload handling (blobs vs. skip offline)

**Skip for now:**
- Full offline mutation queue (Phase 1 scope is reads + UI only)
- Service worker caching of Supabase auth/Realtime channels (doesn't make sense)
- Optimistic UI updates (requires useMutation refactor first)

### Risks

- UTM conversion requires network (fetching monthly UTM value) — can't create UTM expenses offline even with queue
- Receipt uploads are blobs — IndexedDB can store them but localStorage can't
- Multiple sequential DB writes per expense mean the mutation queue needs transaction-like semantics
- SW cache invalidation: stale Supabase data could show on hard refresh if we cache too aggressively (mitigation: short TTL or cache-first with background revalidation)

### Ready for Proposal
Yes

observations.title: Diagnosed Supabase env failure on Workers deploy
observations.content:
**What**: The deployed Worker can throw `Missing Supabase environment variable(s): SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` because the app reads Supabase credentials from `import.meta.env.VITE_SUPABASE_*` at build time or `process.env.SUPABASE_*` at Worker runtime, while the CI workflow deploys before uploading Worker secrets.
**Why**: User reported the startup error after deploying to Cloudflare Workers.
**Where**: `src/integrations/supabase/client.ts`, `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, `wrangler.jsonc`.
**Learned**: `wrangler secret put` creates/deploys a new Worker version; a safer CI path is to ensure Cloudflare secrets exist before deploy or deploy with a secrets file, and to add `secrets.required` in `wrangler.jsonc` so deploy fails early when required secrets are absent.

observations.title: Fixed Cloudflare Workers deploy secrets flow
observations.content:
**What**: Added `secrets.required` to `wrangler.jsonc` for Supabase runtime secrets and changed GitHub Actions deploy to use the generated `dist/server/wrangler.json` with `--secrets-file`.
**Why**: The Worker was starting without `SUPABASE_URL`/`SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`; deploying from the generated TanStack/Cloudflare build config preserves static asset wiring and uploads secrets with the code version.
**Where**: `wrangler.jsonc`, `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`.
**Learned**: For this TanStack Start + Cloudflare Vite build, root `wrangler.jsonc` is the source config, but the deploy target should be the generated `dist/server/wrangler.json` after `pnpm build` because it points `main` to `index.js` and `assets.directory` to `../client`.

observations.title: Fixed circular dependency loop in offline connectivity hooks
observations.content:
**What**: Fixed the circular dependency loop in offline hooks that was causing the app to get stuck displaying "Sin conexión" (Offline) even when connected. Unified hook state under a single source of truth.
**Why**: The `processQueueNow` callback depended on the `isOnline` state, while the event listener `useEffect` (which updates `isOnline`) depended on `processQueueNow`. This circular loop caused event listeners to continuously bind/unbind and kept the connectivity state fluctuating or stuck. Additionally, `useOffline` and `useOfflineMutationQueue` had duplicate listeners and state, getting out of sync.
**Where**: `src/hooks/use-offline-mutation-queue.ts`, `src/hooks/use-offline.ts`
**Learned**: Breaking reactive loops is critical: read browser APIs like `navigator.onLine` directly inside callback functions rather than pointing them to state dependencies to keep callbacks stable. Unifying multiple hooks under a single state wrapper eliminates timing race conditions.

observations.title: Fixed SSR crash from inverted hook dependency direction
observations.content:
**What**: Fixed SSR crash and offline state bug caused by incorrect hook dependency direction in offline hooks.
**Why**: `useOffline` was calling `useOfflineMutationQueue()`, which depends on `useAuth()` and `useQueryClient()`. When `OfflineBanner` rendered during SSR, it crashed because (1) the Supabase client throws without env vars on the server, and (2) QueryClientProvider doesn't exist in SSR context. Additionally, the circular dependency between `processQueueNow` ↔ `isOnline` caused the offline banner to get stuck showing "Sin conexión" even when online.
**Where**: `src/hooks/use-offline.ts`, `src/hooks/use-offline-mutation-queue.ts`
**Learned**: NEVER make a leaf/utility hook (like `useOffline`) depend on provider-dependent hooks (auth, query client, routing). The dependency direction must always flow DOWN: standalone hooks → provider-dependent hooks → consumer components. For SSR-safe hooks, only use `useState` + `useEffect` with `typeof window` guards. For online/offline transition detection, use a `useRef` to track previous state instead of circular state dependencies.

observations.title: Fixed offline banner false positive + recurring_expenses 403
observations.content:
**What**: Fixed two bugs: offline banner false positive + recurring_expenses 403 RLS error **Why**: 1. `useOffline` hook used complex fetch-based connectivity checks that failed due to CORS (Supabase returns 401, browser blocks response reading). Simplified to browser online/offline events only, defaulting to online. 2. `useCreateRecurring` mutation didn't include `created_by` in the insert, causing RLS policy violation (`auth.uid() = created_by`). **Where**: - `src/hooks/use-offline.ts` — simplified to browser events only, default online - `src/hooks/use-recurring.ts` — added `created_by: user?.id` to recurring_expenses insert - `src/routes/app.gastos.nuevo.tsx` — fixed FormLabel outside FormField (line 353) - `src/lib/utm.ts` — fixed `formatUtm` to use `toFixed(2)` instead of `toFixed(1)` for decimal UTM amounts **Learned**: - CORS blocks `fetch` responses from being read — browser shows 401 in DevTools but `fetch` throws in catch block. Don't use fetch for connectivity checks against cross-origin APIs. - `navigator.onLine` + browser events is the simplest and most reliable offline detection. Default to online to avoid false positives. - Always include `created_by` / `owner_id` in RLS-protected inserts. - `FormLabel` from shadcn requires `` context — use `

` for standalone labels.

observations.title: Fixed 6 P0 critical bugs in wootric-saas
observations.content:
**What**: Fixed 6 critical (P0) bugs across the wootric-saas codebase

**Why**: Code review identified critical bugs in security, data integrity, and correctness

**Where**: 
- `src/infrastructure/auth/InvitationService.ts` — Fixed broken `admin.rpc()` inside `.update()`, fixed quota_key mismatch ("users" → "max_users")
- `src/application/services/SubscriptionService.ts` — Reordered changePlan to create new subscription BEFORE canceling old one (atomicity improvement)
- `src/application/services/QuotaService.ts` — Added atomic increment via PostgreSQL RPC with read-then-write fallback
- `src/infrastructure/auth/RegistrationService.ts` — Removed hardcoded JWT secret fallback, now throws if JWT_SECRET env var is missing
- `workers/export-worker/src/index.ts` — Added table name allowlist and regex sanitization to prevent SQL injection via PostgREST
- `src/application/services/__tests__/SubscriptionService.test.ts` — Updated mock to support `neq()` and `maybeSingle()`, updated changePlan test

**Learned**: 
- Supabase JS client doesn't support transactions — use RPC for atomic operations
- `.rpc()` can't be used inside `.update()` — it's not a valid value expression
- Always sanitize table names before concatenating into PostgREST URLs
- Never hardcode secrets as fallbacks — fail loudly instead

observations.title: PostgreSQL reserved keyword "limit" requires quoting
observations.content:
**What**: Fixed SQL syntax error when creating `increment_quota` function — `limit` is a reserved keyword in PostgreSQL

**Why**: The initial SQL used bare `limit` column name which PostgreSQL rejected with syntax error 42601

**Where**: PostgreSQL migration for `increment_quota` function on `usage_quotas` table

**Learned**: In PostgreSQL, always double-quote reserved words used as column names (e.g., `"limit"`). The `usage_quotas` table uses `limit` as a column name which conflicts with the `LIMIT` clause keyword. This applies to any SQL referencing this column — Drizzle schema handles it automatically, but raw SQL and RPC functions need explicit quoting.

observations.title: Fixed 6 P1 security and stability issues in middleware + WootricService
observations.content:
**What**: Fixed 6 P1 security and stability issues across middleware and WootricService

**Why**: Code review identified security vulnerabilities and stability risks

**Where**: 
- `src/middleware.ts` — Removed global `debugInfo` (race condition), CSRF now rejects with 403, debug headers only in dev, removed X-User-Permissions from response headers, extracted helpers to reduce complexity
- `src/application/services/WootricService.ts` — Added max retry limit (2) to prevent infinite recursion on 401/429
- `workers/sync-worker/src/wootric-client.ts` — Same max retry fix for 429 recursion

**Learned**:
- Global mutable state in middleware is dangerous in serverless — use local variables returned from functions
- CSRF that doesn't reject is worse than no CSRF — it gives false sense of security
- Debug headers (X-Debug-*, X-User-Permissions) in production are information leaks
- Recursive API calls without retry limits can cause worker crashes and infinite loops

observations.title: Fixed Cloudflare deploy — all infrastructure auto-created
observations.content:
**What**: Fixed Cloudflare Workers deploy pipeline — 5 sequential failures resolved

**Why**: Deploy was failing on: missing Cloudflare type imports, wrong KV namespace IDs, missing queues, missing sub-worker service bindings, invalid cron string

**Where**: 
- `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` — complete rewrite with ensure-infra + sub-worker deploys
- `.github/scripts/ensure-infra.sh` — auto-creates KV namespaces, R2, queues + patches wrangler.jsonc
- `src/middleware.ts`, `src/infrastructure/storage/R2StorageService.ts`, `src/lib/cloudflare/bindings.ts` — explicit CF type imports
- `workers/sync-worker/wrangler.jsonc` — cron day-of-week 0→7

**Learned**:
- Next.js 16 + Turbopack does NOT resolve ambient types from `worker-configuration.d.ts` — ALL Cloudflare types (KVNamespace, R2Bucket, Fetcher, Queue, MessageBatch) need explicit `import type` from `@cloudflare/workers-types`
- KV namespace IDs in wrangler.jsonc must match the actual Cloudflare account — use ensure-infra.sh to auto-resolve
- Cloudflare cron API rejects day-of-week `0` for Sunday — must use `7`
- Service bindings (EXPORT_WORKER, SYNC_WORKER) require the referenced Workers to exist BEFORE deploying the main worker
- Cloudflare API can be flaky for queue creation — retry with 5s delay works

observations.content:
**What**: Fixed VacationRequestModal step2 sizing — modal now adapts to content on both desktop and mobile

**Why**: The modal had hardcoded minHeight (710px desktop, 980px mobile) via inline style, causing extra space below buttons. Step1 (form) remained in DOM during step2 with position:relative + translateX(-100%), keeping form height in flow. - Key CSS rules for .vacation-request-steps.salter:

observations.title: framer-motion tree-shaking applied across 25 files
observations.content:
**What**: Replaced `import { motion } from "framer-motion"` with `import { div } from "framer-motion/m"` and replaced `<motion.div>` with `<div>` in 25 files. For 6 files that also use AnimatePresence, split the import into two: `{ div } from "framer-motion/m"` and `{ AnimatePresence } from "framer-motion"`.

**Why**: The `motion` object is a Proxy that dynamically creates components for ALL HTML elements (~80+), preventing tree-shaking and bloating the vendor-ui chunk to 530KB.

**Where**: 19 Category A files (motion only) + 6 Category B files (motion + AnimatePresence) across src/pages/ and src/components/admin/

**Learned**: The `<motion.div` → `<div` replaceAll also matches `</motion.div>` since `<motion.div` is a substring of `</motion.div>` — no separate closing tag replacement was needed for those cases. Build succeeded and vendor-ui dropped from ~530KB to ~413KB (22% reduction).

observations.title: P1 completado: framer-motion tree shaking
observations.content:
**What**: Reemplacé imports de `framer-motion` por elementos individuales de `framer-motion/m` en 25 archivos. vendor-ui bajó de 530KB a 404KB (-126KB, 24%).
**Why**: El objeto `motion` es un Proxy que impide tree-shaking porque el bundler no puede saber qué elementos HTML se usarán en runtime.
**Where**: 25 archivos .tsx (6 con AnimatePresence separado, 19 con solo `{ div } from "framer-motion/m"`)
**Learned**: framer-motion v12 no exporta `motion` desde `/m` — exporta elementos individuales (`div`, `span`, etc.). Para AnimatePresence no hay sub-entry, queda importado del bundle principal. En la práctica, los 6 archivos que usan AnimatePresence siguen importando framer-motion principal, pero el tree-shaking del bundler evita duplicar el código compartido.

observations.title: Fixed virtualizer test failures with @tanstack/react-virtual mock
observations.content:
**What**: Fixed ScoresPage, FinancePage, and AdminPage tests failing after adding @tanstack/react-virtual v3 virtualization. The fix: (1) changed scroll containers from `maxHeight: calc(100vh - X)` to `height: calc(100vh - X)` with `minHeight: 400px` for prod, and (2) mocked `@tanstack/react-virtual` in test setup to render ALL items (no virtualization) because JSDOM can't compute CSS calc() values.
**Why**: JSDOM returns 0 for `getBoundingClientRect()` on elements with `calc()` heights, so the virtualizer measured 0 container height and rendered no items. Tests expected items to be visible.
**Where**: src/test/setup.tsx (added vi.mock for @tanstack/react-virtual), src/pages/AdminPage.tsx, src/pages/ScoresPage.tsx, src/pages/FinancePage.tsx (changed maxHeight to height + minHeight)
**Learned**: `@tanstack/react-virtual` v3 uses ResizeObserver internally and relies on container measurement. In JSDOM, CSS `calc()` is never computed, so the container always has 0 clientHeight. The mock approach is cleaner than trying to make JSDOM compute layout — the virtualizer mock returns all items synchronously, which is correct for test behavior (we don't need to test virtualization itself, only that items render correctly).

observations.title: Session summary: archery-club-hub
observations.content:
## Goal
Add virtual scrolling with `@tanstack/react-virtual` v3 to AdminPage (desktop table + mobile cards), ScoresPage (mobile cards), and FinancePage (desktop table + mobile cards)

## Instructions
- Tests must pass (all 137). TrainingSessionsPage pre-existing QRCode failures are acceptable.
- Virtual scrolling wraps existing lists without changing item rendering logic, styles, or behavior.
- Desktop tables use flex-based `<TableRow>` with `position: absolute` because virtualizer requires absolute positioning.

## Discoveries
- JSDOM cannot compute CSS `calc()` values, so elements with `height: calc(100vh - 300px)` always have `clientHeight = 0`. The virtualizer then measures 0 container size and renders no items.
- `@tanstack/react-virtual` v3 internally uses `new ResizeObserver(cb)` in `observeElementRect()`, which requires a proper class-based mock (not `vi.fn().mockImplementation(...)`).
- The virtualizer re-render from ResizeObserver is async (React 18 batching), so even with correct measurement, the items aren't available in the synchronous test render.
- The cleanest solution: mock `@tanstack/react-virtual` in test setup to render ALL items synchronously — tests shouldn't test virtualization behavior, only that items render correctly.
- Changed `maxHeight` to `height` with `minHeight` fallback for production: `height: calc(100vh - 300px)` with `minHeight: 400px`. This ensures the container always has a defined height regardless of viewport.

## Accomplished
- ✅ Modified AdminPage.tsx: Changed mobile container from `maxHeight: calc(100vh - 300px)` to `height: calc(100vh - 300px)` with `minHeight: 400px`
- ✅ Modified ScoresPage.tsx: Same change for scores list container
- ✅ Modified FinancePage.tsx: Same change for both desktop table and mobile card containers
- ✅ Added `@tanstack/react-virtual` mock in src/test/setup.tsx that renders ALL items synchronously (no virtualization in tests)
- ✅ Simplified ResizeObserver mock (no longer needs to fire measurement callbacks)
- ✅ Build passes (1.97s)
- ✅ 133/137 tests pass, only 4 pre-existing TrainingSessionsPage QRCode failures remain

## Next Steps

**What**: Completed the framer-motion div → MotionDiv migration across all 24+ files. observations.title: Session summary: archery-club-hub
observations.content:
## Goal
Fix all remaining strictNullChecks + noImplicitAny TypeScript errors (~76) across the archery-club-hub codebase to get to 0 errors, with build and tests passing.

## Instructions
- Never use // @ts-ignore or // @ts-expect-error — prefer proper type fixes
- Prefer optional chaining (`?.`), nullish coalescing (`??`), and early returns over type assertions
- After fixes: verify with `npx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit`, build, and test

## Discoveries
- Interface inheritance (extends) is strict: redeclaring inherited fields with different nullability (e.g., `grace_days?: number` vs `grace_days: number | null`) causes TS2430 — remove redeclared fields from the extending interface
- Spreading potentially-null objects (`{ ...(settings ?? {}), ... }`) erases required fields — use early return guards (`if (!settings) return <error>`) so TypeScript narrows the type
- Supabase RPC calls with non-generated function names need `as never` for BOTH the function name AND the args object
- `club_id` in Supabase generated types is often `string | null` — many manual interfaces had it as `string`, causing cascading assignment errors (16 in AdminPage alone)
- framer-motion v12 requires `{ div as MotionDiv }` import from "framer-motion/m" — not `import { motion }`
- `qrcode` package exists in node_modules but wasn't imported in TrainingSessionsPage.tsx — causing TSC2304

observations.title: Vercel + pnpm frozen-lockfile error solution
observations.content:
**What**: Fixed Vercel deploy failing with ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE after moving @prisma/client to devDependencies

**Why**: Vercel runs `pnpm install` with frozen-lockfile by default in CI. When package.json changes without updating pnpm-lock.yaml, the lockfile doesn't match and the build fails.

**Where**: pnpm-lock.yaml regenerated with `pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile` and committed

**Learned**: 
- Every time package.json changes (dependencies/devDependencies/scripts), ALWAYS run `pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile` and commit the lockfile
- The error says "Cannot install with frozen-lockfile because pnpm-lock.yaml is not up to date" — that's the key message
- To check locally if lockfile is stale: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (will fail same as Vercel)

observations.title: sdd/tracker-marking-ux/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: Tracker Sticker Marking UX

## Intent

Fix critical performance and UX issues on `/tracker` where clicking a sticker produces zero visual feedback for 5+ seconds due to missing `useMemo` dependencies, no optimistic update for duplicate marking, and silent errors. Users currently have no way to tell if their click registered.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Fix `useMemo` dep arrays to re-compute `ownedSet` and `trackerData` immediately on toggle
- Add optimistic update to `incrementDuplicateMutation` with rollback on error
- Add toast notifications for mutation success/error
- Reduce debounce queue from 5s to 1s for responsive feel

### Out of Scope
- "Limpiar" confirmation dialog (stretch goal)
- Double-click detection refinement (deferred)
- Extra DB query removal (`getById()` — separate infra change)
- Excessive query invalidation scope reduction (deferred)

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
None — all changes are performance/UX fixes to existing tracker behavior in `src/presentation/hooks/` and `src/app/(dashboard)/tracker/`.

### Modified Capabilities
None — no existing specs in `openspec/specs/`.

## Approach

1. **useMemo deps fix** (`useTracker.ts`): Add `toggleVersion` state variable to both `ownedSet` and `data` memo dependency arrays. This makes `buildTrackerData()` and `ownedSet` re-run on every toggle click via the `setToggleVersion(v => v + 1)` call already in `enqueue()`.
2. **Optimistic duplicate update** (`useCollection.ts`): Add `onMutate` to `incrementDuplicateMutation` that immediately increments `duplicateCount` in the cached collection, with `onError` rollback restoring previous state — same pattern as `addStickerMutation`.
3. **Toast feedback**: Add `sonner` toast calls in mutation lifecycle hooks (`onSuccess`, `onError`) for add/remove/duplicate operations. Mount `<Toaster />` in the tracker layout.
4. **Debounce reduction**: Lower `DEBOUNCE_MS` from 5000 to 1000 in `useTracker.ts`.

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `src/presentation/hooks/useTracker.ts` | Modified | Fix useMemo deps; reduce DEBOUNCE_MS |
| `src/presentation/hooks/useCollection.ts` | Modified | Add optimistic update + toast hooks to duplicate mutation |
| `src/app/(dashboard)/tracker/layout.tsx` | Modified | Add `<Toaster />` wrapper |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| `sonner` not installed / breaking build | Low | Add dep first, test build before launch |
| Optimistic rollback causes UI flicker | Low | Test with throttled network in devtools |
| 1s debounce increases DB write frequency | Low | Upsert is idempotent — no data corruption risk |

## Rollback Plan

Revert the three affected files. No schema, infrastructure, or DB changes involved — pure TypeScript revert.

## Dependencies

- `sonner` toast library (add to `package.json`)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Sticker click shows visual opacity/pulse change within <100ms
- [ ] Duplicate count increments immediately on click without server round-trip
- [ ] Toast notification appears on mutation success and error
- [ ] All existing tests pass (`pnpm test`)

observations.title: Session summary: tappmesa
observations.content:
## Goal
Realizar una revisión completa del proyecto TappMesa (React + Vite + Supabase) con lente mobile-first, identificar oportunidades de mejora, y ejecutar fixes de alto impacto.

## Instructions
- El user habla español rioplatense (voseo). Usar "vos", "dale", "vamo'", "ahí está"
- Es descontracturado pero profesional — responde con la misma energía
- Prefiere acciones concretas a teoría
- Mobile-first es la prioridad del proyecto
- Siempre mantener sesión summary para continuar después

## Discoveries
- **Auth crítica**: `secureAuthDirect.js` hace hashing client-side con SHA-256 + fallback a hash casero de 32 bits + texto plano. La sal está hardcodeada (`tappmesa-salt-2024`). Las API routes con bcrypt existen pero no se usan — el frontend saltea los endpoints y va directo a Supabase.
- **@prisma/client es código muerto**: `src/lib/prisma.ts` existe pero NADIE lo importa. No está en la API de Vercel, no en scripts, no en frontend. Build lo tree-shakea bien pero es ruido peligroso.
- **La app no es PWA**: sin service worker, sin manifest, sin offline support. Para mobile-first, es la oportunidad más grande.
- **Bundle audit completado**: index.js se redujo de 66 kB a 8 kB (raw) con el fix de lazy loading.
- **Vercel + pnpm frozen-lockfile**: cada vez que se cambia package.json hay que regenerar el lockfile con `pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile` y comitearlo.
- **Tests**: 50 tests pasan, los context tests tienen issues pre-existentes con mocking de Supabase.
- **PR #139 creado** en branch `perf/lazy-loading-and-deps-cleanup`

## Accomplished
- ✅ Bundle audit completo con Vite build (10 chunks analizados)
- ✅ Fix lazy loading: 4 páginas convertidas de import estático a lazy
- ✅ @prisma/client movido de dependencies a devDependencies
- ✅ Lockfile regenerado y comiteado
- ✅ PR #139 creado + pusheado
- ✅ Documentados hallazgos clave en Engram

## Next Steps
- 🔲 **Auth**: Migrar `secureAuthDirect.js` a usar las API routes con bcrypt. Este es EL issue más crítico.
- 🔲 **Service Worker**: Implementar PWA con workbox para caching de menú y offline fallback.
- 🔲 **Separar supabase.js**: Romper el God Object de 588 líneas en servicios individuales.
- 🔲 **TypeScript**: Arrancar migración por `src/lib/` y `src/utils/`.
- 🔲 **Re-auditar bundle** después de implementar más cambios.
- 🔲 **Fix tests de context** (mocking de Supabase roto).

## Relevant Files
- src/lib/secureAuthDirect.js — Auth client-side insegura, hashing de 32 bits + texto plano
- src/lib/supabase.js — God Object de 588 líneas, mezcla auth/orders/menu/analytics/clientes/notificaciones
- src/lib/prisma.ts — Código muerto, nada lo importa
- src/context/TenantContext.jsx — 397 líneas mezclando URL parsing, carga de tenant, sesiones de mesa, branding
- src/components/SecureAdminApp.jsx — 601 líneas, monolito con sidebar + routing + permisos
- src/App.jsx — Router principal, lazy loading fixeado
- src/components/LazyComponents.jsx — Lazy exports, ahora incluye todas las páginas
- api/auth/signin.js, signup.js — Endpoints con bcrypt que NO se están usando desde el frontend

observations.title: sdd/tracker-marking-ux/spec-pr2
observations.content:
# PR 2 — Toast + Optimistic Duplicate

Domain: tracker (sticker marking UX). Part of the `tracker-marking-ux` change.

## Requirements

### R1: Optimistic duplicate increment

When the user marks a sticker as duplicate, the count badge MUST increment immediately. On API failure, it MUST revert to the previous value.

#### Scenarios

- **Happy path**: GIVEN `duplicateCount = 0` WHEN double-clicked THEN badge shows `1` immediately AND no flicker after server responds
- **Error rollback**: GIVEN `duplicateCount = 2` WHEN API fails THEN badge reverts to `2` AND error toast appears
- **Rapid multi-click**: GIVEN three stickers with `duplicateCount = 0` WHEN double-clicked within 500ms THEN each increments independently without cross-contamination

### R2: Toast on mutation lifecycle

The system SHALL show a toast on success and on error for all three sticker operations (add, remove, duplicate). `<Toaster />` SHALL be mounted once in the tracker route tree.

#### Scenarios

- **Success — add**: GIVEN sticker is `missing` WHEN single-click AND API succeeds THEN success toast appears
- **Success — remove**: GIVEN sticker is `obtained` WHEN single-click AND API succeeds THEN success toast appears
- **Success — duplicate**: GIVEN `duplicateCount = 0` WHEN double-click AND API succeeds THEN success toast appears
- **Error — any mutation**: GIVEN any mutation WHEN API fails THEN error toast with descriptive message appears (e.g. "Error al marcar sticker")
- **Combined rollback + error**: GIVEN optimistic duplicate applied WHEN API fails THEN count reverts AND error toast appears

### R3: Toast auto-dismiss

Success toasts SHOULD dismiss after 3s. Error toasts SHOULD dismiss within 3–5s.

#### Scenario

- GIVEN a success toast visible WHEN 3s elapse THEN toast is removed

### R4: `<Toaster />` mounting

`<Toaster />` SHALL render on `/tracker` and all its sub-routes (`/tracker/missing`, `/tracker/duplicates`).

#### Scenario

- GIVEN user navigates to any `/tracker/*` route WHEN a mutation fires THEN the toast renders correctly

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Duplicate count badge updates in <100ms of double-click
2. Failed duplicate API call reverts badge AND shows error toast
3. All three operations (add, remove, duplicate) produce success toast on API success
4. All three operations produce error toast on API failure
5. Success toasts auto-dismiss within 3 ± 0.5s
6. `<Toaster />` renders on `/tracker`, `/tracker/missing`, `/tracker/duplicates`
7. Rapid double-click on multiple stickers — no race conditions
8. `sonner` is already in `package.json` (no new dep)

## Non-functional

| # | Requirement | Threshold |
|---|-------------|-----------|
| 1 | Optimistic update latency | <100ms click → badge |
| 2 | Success toast duration | 3s ± 0.5s |
| 3 | Error toast duration | 3–5s |
| 4 | Toaster position | Bottom-right (default) |
| 5 | Toaster theme | Match system (dark/light) |

observations.title: sdd/tracker-marking-ux/spec-pr1
observations.content:
# Delta for Tracker Marking UX — PR 1

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Immediate Sticker Toggle Feedback

When a user clicks a sticker in the tracker view, the visual state (obtained/missing) MUST update within 100ms without waiting for the debounced server flush.

The system MUST recompute `ownedSet` and `trackerData` on every local toggle via `toggleVersion` — adding the current `toggleVersion` state value as a dependency to both `useMemo` arrays in `useTracker.ts`.

(New behavior — previously `useMemo` dep arrays omitted `toggleVersion`, so the local toggle triggered a re-render but `useMemo` returned stale values.)

#### Scenario: Single click marks sticker as obtained

- GIVEN the tracker page is loaded with collection data
- WHEN the user clicks an unmarked sticker
- THEN the sticker visually transitions to "obtained" state within 100ms
- AND the group owned count increments immediately
- AND an `add` mutation is queued for debounced flush

#### Scenario: Click toggles sticker back to missing

- GIVEN a sticker is currently in "obtained" state
- WHEN the user clicks that sticker
- THEN the sticker visually transitions to "missing" state within 100ms
- AND a `remove` mutation is queued for debounced flush
- AND the group owned count decrements immediately

#### Scenario: Rapid toggling of five stickers within 2 seconds

- GIVEN the tracker page is loaded
- WHEN the user clicks 5 different stickers over a 2-second interval
- THEN each sticker updates its visual state within 100ms of its respective click
- AND the debounce timer resets on each click
- AND exactly one `flushQueue` execution fires 1000ms after the last click
- AND all 5 mutations are sent in that single flush

### Requirement: Debounce Flush at 1000ms

The debounce delay `DEBOUNCE_MS` MUST be reduced from 5000ms to 1000ms.

(Previously: `DEBOUNCE_MS = 5000`)

#### Scenario: Flush fires after 1s of inactivity

- GIVEN a sticker has been toggled
- WHEN 1000ms elapses with no further clicks
- THEN `flushQueue` executes, sending queued mutations to the server
- AND `localToggles` is cleared

#### Scenario: New click resets debounce timer

- GIVEN a sticker was toggled 500ms ago
- WHEN another sticker is toggled
- THEN the debounce timer resets to 1000ms from this latest click

## Acceptance Criteria

| # | Criterion | Verification |
|---|-----------|-------------|
| 1 | Visual state change within 100ms of click | `performance.now()` measurement in DevTools |
| 2 | Server flush fires 1000ms (±100ms) after last click | Timer log in test or DevTools |
| 3 | `buildTrackerData` and `ownedSet` re-compute on every toggle | No stale values after `setToggleVersion(v => v + 1)` |
| 4 | All existing tests pass | `pnpm test` exits 0 |

## Non-functional

- **UI response**: <100ms from click event to DOM update (`requestAnimationFrame` callback)
- **Debounce precision**: ±100ms tolerance on 1000ms `setTimeout`
- **Bundle impact**: Zero — no new imports or dependencies for PR 1

observations.content:
**What**: Implemented PR 2 of tracker-marking-ux: optimistic duplicate increment with rollback, toast notifications on all mutation lifecycles, and ToasterProvider mounting on /tracker routes.

**Why**: User feedback loop improvement — immediate visual feedback on duplicate click, toast confirmations for all sticker operations, and proper error recovery.

**Where**: 
- `src/presentation/hooks/collection-mutations.ts` (NEW) — pure function `applyOptimisticDuplicate` + `showMutationToast` + `MUTATION_MESSAGES` constants

**Learned**: TanStack React Query v5 removed `onSuccess` from `useMutation` options; used `onSettled` with error check instead. The existing `addStickerMutation` onMutate/onError rollback pattern was replicable for `incrementDuplicateMutation`. For TDD in node environment without jsdom, extracting pure functions was the cleanest approach — avoided needing renderHook or DOM setup.

observations.title: VacationRequestModal: conditional scrollBehavior to prevent unnecessary scrollbar
observations.content:
**What**: Changed scrollBehavior in VacationRequestModal to be conditional based on step

**Why**: The modal's `.vacation-request-steps.salter` CSS had missing `position: absolute` on `.step1` (caused content to leak through and take up 260px height), `overflow: hidden` clipped content, and `scrollBehavior` switching caused Atlaskit to remount.

**Where**:

- `assets/src/js/apps/vacations/myrequests/components/VacationRequestResumen.jsx` — m-t-0, removed m-b-40, minHeight

**Learned**: `visibility: hidden` on a parent doesn't hide children with explicit `visibility: visible` (common in library components like datepickers/buttons). Use `display: none` + `position: absolute` instead. Also, changing `scrollBehavior` prop conditionally causes Atlaskit to remount CustomBody internally.

observations.content:
## Goal
Fix vacation request modal layout issues — buttons hidden for non-EC countries, step 1 content bleeding into step 2, scrollbar appearing unnecessarily.

## Instructions
- Use `display: none` + `position: absolute` to completely remove step 1 from flow/layout when hidden, not `visibility: hidden`
- Keep `scrollBehavior="inside"` fixed to avoid Atlaskit CustomBody remount issues
- User prefers to NOT use conditional rendering `{step === 1 && (...)}` — stick with CSS-only approach for hiding step1

## Discoveries
- `visibility: hidden` on parent does NOT override children that explicitly set `visibility: visible` (common in form inputs, datepickers, buttons from libraries)
- Atlaskit's Modal with `CustomBody` (which uses `useState(false)` + `useEffect(() => setShow(true), [])`) can break when `scrollBehavior` changes between renders — the body remounts and the state gets lost
- `min-height: auto` vs `min-height: 0` matters in flex contexts for preventing unnecessary scrollbars

## Accomplished
- ✅ Fixed `.step1` CSS: added `position: absolute` + `display: none` to prevent content leaking into step 2
- ✅ Fixed `.step2` CSS: `position: relative`, `min-height: 0`, proper padding
- ✅ Changed `scrollBehavior` from conditional to fixed `"inside"`
- ✅ Fixed `.view-steps` overrides: `overflow: visible`, `min-height: 0`, `margin: 0`

- None — the modal layout is resolved for all countries

observations.title: sdd/fix-auth-client-bcrypt/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: fix-auth-client-bcrypt

## Intent

Eliminar un backdoor crítico de seguridad: `src/lib/secureAuthDirect.js` bypassea bcrypt usando SHA-256 con salt estático, un fallback hash de 32 bits colisionable, y comparación en texto plano. `src/lib/supabase.js` delega todo `authService` a ese archivo, anulando el sistema bcrypt implementado en las API routes serverless.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Eliminar `src/lib/secureAuthDirect.js` (406 líneas, código inseguro)
- Refactorizar `authService` en `src/lib/supabase.js` para llamar a API routes via fetch
- Preservar `getTrialStatus()` (usa Supabase client directo, no auth)
- Todos los tests existentes de auth deben seguir pasando

### Out of Scope
- Migrar hashes existentes en DB (se maneja vía password reset)
- Refactor de otros servicios (`orderService`, `menuService`, etc.)
- Cambios en la API de AuthContext (interfaz pública no cambia)
- Migrar a Supabase Auth nativo

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
None — pure refactor. Auth interface (signIn, signUp, signOut, getCurrentSession) no cambia.

### Modified Capabilities
None — no cambian requerimientos a nivel spec.

## Approach

1. **Eliminar** `src/lib/secureAuthDirect.js` por completo
2. **Refactorizar** `authService` en `supabase.js`:
   - Cada método (`signIn`, `signUp`, `signOut`, `getCurrentSession`) hace `fetch()` a `/api/auth/{endpoint}`
   - `signIn` → POST `/api/auth/signin` con `{ email, password }`
   - `signUp` → POST `/api/auth/signup` con `{ email, password, ownerName, restaurantName, ... }`
   - `getCurrentSession` → GET `/api/auth/session` con `Authorization: Bearer {token}`
   - `signOut` → POST `/api/auth/signout` con token en header
   - `getTrialStatus` se mantiene igual (usa supabase client directo)
3. **Gestionar session token** en localStorage con el mismo key `tappmesa-session`
4. **Error handling**: wrappear respuestas de API al formato que AuthContext espera (`{ success, admin, tenant, sessionToken, error }`)

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `src/lib/secureAuthDirect.js` | Removed | Archivo completo eliminado |
| `src/lib/supabase.js` | Modified | authService.replace() con fetch-based impl |
| `api/auth/signin.js` | Unchanged | Referencia — test de integración |
| `api/auth/signup.js` | Unchanged | Referencia — test de integración |
| `api/auth/session.js` | Unchanged | Referencia — test de integración |
| `api/auth/signout.js` | Unchanged | Referencia — test de integración |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| API routes no disponibles (Vercel cold start) | Med | Timeout corto + error claro al usuario |
| Formato respuesta API distinto al esperado | Low | Tests de integración contra API real |
| getTrialStatus usa supabase nullable (line 7-14) | Low | Se mantiene igual, no tocar |

## Rollback Plan

Restaurar `src/lib/secureAuthDirect.js` desde git (`git restore src/lib/secureAuthDirect.js`) y revertir cambios en `src/lib/supabase.js`. El auth vuelve a funcionar con el servicio directo.

## Dependencies

- Ninguna. `bcryptjs` ya está en `package.json` (server-side).
- API routes deben estar deployadas en Vercel y accesibles desde el frontend.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `secureAuthDirect.js` ya no existe en el código
- [ ] `authService.signIn()` llama a POST `/api/auth/signin` y retorna session token
- [ ] `authService.signUp()` llama a POST `/api/auth/signup` y crea tenant+admin
- [ ] `authService.getCurrentSession()` usa GET `/api/auth/session` con token Bearer
- [ ] `authService.signOut()` llama a POST `/api/auth/signout`
- [ ] `getTrialStatus()` sigue funcionando sin cambios
- [ ] AuthContext.login/register/logout funcionan sin errores
- [ ] Todos los tests existentes pasan

observations.title: sdd/fix-auth-client-bcrypt/spec
observations.content:
# Spec: auth-service — Refactor to API Routes

## Context

Refactor puro de `authService` en `src/lib/supabase.js`. `secureAuthDirect.js` (SHA-256 con salt estático + fallback hash 32-bit + comparación en texto plano) se reemplaza con llamadas `fetch()` a las API routes serverless que usan bcrypt. La interfaz pública (`signIn`, `signUp`, `signOut`, `getCurrentSession`, `getTrialStatus`) NO cambia.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: AUTH-API-01 — signIn via POST /api/auth/signin

`authService.signIn(email, password)` MUST llamar a `POST /api/auth/signin` con body `{ email, password }`. En éxito, MUST guardar `sessionToken` en `localStorage['tappmesa-session']` y retornar `{ success, admin, tenant, sessionToken }`.

#### Scenario: Login exitoso
- GIVEN email y password válidos de un admin activo
- WHEN `authService.signIn(email, password)` se ejecuta
- THEN fetch POST `/api/auth/signin` con `{ email, password }`
- AND recibe 200 con `{ success: true, admin, tenant, sessionToken }`
- AND persiste `sessionToken` en `localStorage['tappmesa-session']`
- AND retorna `{ success: true, admin, tenant, sessionToken }`

#### Scenario: Credenciales inválidas
- GIVEN email inexistente o password incorrecto
- WHEN `authService.signIn(email, password)` se ejecuta
- THEN recibe 401 con `{ error }`
- AND retorna `{ success: false, error }` sin modificar localStorage

#### Scenario: Error de red / cold start
- GIVEN la API route no responde (timeout, network failure)
- WHEN `authService.signIn(email, password)` se ejecuta
- THEN atrapa el error del fetch
- AND retorna `{ success: false, error: "Error de conexión. Intenta nuevamente." }`

### Requirement: AUTH-API-02 — signUp via POST /api/auth/signup

`authService.signUp(userData)` MUST llamar a `POST /api/auth/signup` con `{ email, password, ownerName, restaurantName, ... }`. En éxito, MUST guardar `sessionToken` en localStorage y retornar la respuesta completa con `trialInfo`.

#### Scenario: Registro exitoso
- GIVEN datos completos de registro
- WHEN `authService.signUp(userData)` se ejecuta
- THEN fetch POST `/api/auth/signup` con los datos
- AND recibe 201 con `{ success, tenant, admin, sessionToken, trialInfo }`
- AND persiste `sessionToken` en localStorage, retorna el objeto completo

#### Scenario: Email duplicado
- GIVEN un email ya registrado
- WHEN `authService.signUp(userData)` se ejecuta
- THEN recibe 400 con `{ error: "El email ya está registrado" }`
- AND retorna `{ success: false, error }`

### Requirement: AUTH-API-03 — getCurrentSession via GET /api/auth/session

`authService.getCurrentSession()` MUST leer `localStorage['tappmesa-session']`. Si existe token, llama a `GET /api/auth/session` con header `Authorization: Bearer {token}`.

#### Scenario: Sesión válida
- GIVEN token válido en localStorage
- WHEN `getCurrentSession()` se ejecuta
- THEN fetch GET `/api/auth/session` con Bearer token
- AND recibe 200 con `{ admin, tenant, sessionToken }`
- AND retorna el objeto

#### Scenario: Token expirado o inválido
- GIVEN token expirado en localStorage
- WHEN `getCurrentSession()` se ejecuta
- THEN recibe 401
- AND elimina token de localStorage, retorna `null`

#### Scenario: Sin token
- GIVEN no hay token en localStorage
- WHEN `getCurrentSession()` se ejecuta
- THEN retorna `null` sin hacer fetch

### Requirement: AUTH-API-04 — signOut via POST /api/auth/signout

`authService.signOut()` MUST llamar a `POST /api/auth/signout` con `Authorization: Bearer {token}`. Siempre MUST limpiar localStorage, independiente del resultado.

#### Scenario: Logout exitoso
- GIVEN token en localStorage
- WHEN `signOut()` se ejecuta
- THEN fetch POST `/api/auth/signout` con Bearer token
- AND elimina token de localStorage

#### Scenario: Logout sin token o con error de red
- GIVEN cualquier estado (token o no, red disponible o no)
- WHEN `signOut()` se ejecuta
- THEN intenta el fetch (falla silenciosamente si hay error)
- AND siempre elimina `localStorage['tappmesa-session']`
- AND retorna `{ success: true }`

### Requirement: AUTH-API-05 — getTrialStatus preservado

`authService.getTrialStatus(tenantId)` MUST permanecer exactamente como está, usando `supabase.from('tenants').select(...)` directo.

#### Scenario: Sin cambios
- GIVEN tenant ID
- WHEN `getTrialStatus(tenantId)` se ejecuta
- THEN consulta Supabase directamente
- AND retorna `{ endDate, daysLeft, isExpired, isExpiring }` o `null`

### Requirement: AUTH-API-06 — Métodos deprecated preservados

`authService.hashPassword()` y `authService.generateSessionToken()` MUST permanecer como stubs con warnings de deprecación.

## REMOVED Requirements

### Requirement: AUTH-SECURE-DIRECT — Eliminar secureAuthDirect.js

El archivo `src/lib/secureAuthDirect.js` y su import en `src/lib/supabase.js` MUST ser eliminados.

## API Contract

| Método | HTTP | Endpoint | Auth | Request | Response éxito |
|--------|------|----------|------|---------|----------------|
| signIn | POST | /api/auth/signin | — | { email, password } | 200 { success, admin, tenant, sessionToken } |
| signUp | POST | /api/auth/signup | — | { email, password, ownerName, restaurantName, ... } | 201 { success, tenant, admin, sessionToken, trialInfo } |
| getCurrentSession | GET | /api/auth/session | Bearer | — | 200 { admin, tenant, sessionToken } |
| signOut | POST | /api/auth/signout | Bearer | — | 200 { success } |

## Error Mapping

| HTTP | API body | authService retorna |
|------|----------|-------------------|
| 400 | { error } | { success: false, error } |
| 401 | { error } | { success: false, error } |
| 405 | { error } | { success: false, error } |
| 500 | { error } | { success: false, error } |
| Network error | — | { success: false, error: "Error de conexión. Intenta nuevamente." } |

## Edge Cases

| Caso | Comportamiento |
|------|---------------|
| API route en cold start (Vercel) | Fetch puede tardar varios segundos. authService MUST usar timeout implícito (fetch por defecto) y capturar error. |
| Token malformado en localStorage | Se envía como Bearer. API responde 401 → authService limpia localStorage y retorna null/error. |
| Doble signOut | Segundo llamado: no hay token en localStorage → fetch sin header, siempre limpia y retorna { success: true }. |
| Registro con datos inválidos | API valida y responde 400 con mensaje específico. authService propaga el error sin modificar localStorage. |
| Supabase client null | getTrialStatus() y supabase nullable existen antes del cambio. Si supabase es null, getTrialStatus falla silenciosamente (comportamiento preexistente, no se modifica). |
| Fetch lanza excepción | Catch genérico → retorna error amigable. No hay logging interno (el error handling vive en AuthContext). |

observations.title: SDD Design: fix-auth-client-bcrypt
observations.content:
**What**: SDD design for removing secureAuthDirect.js (insecure SHA-256 + fallback hash) and refactoring authService in supabase.js to use fetch() calls to API routes with bcrypt.

**Why**: Eliminate a critical security backdoor where client-side auth bypassed server-side bcrypt. The API routes already implement bcrypt correctly — the client just needs to call them via fetch instead of delegating to the insecure direct service.

**Where**: `openspec/changes/fix-auth-client-bcrypt/design.md`

**Learned**: There's already a `src/lib/authService.js` with a fetch-based SecureAuthService class (207 lines) that was never wired up — the active code in `src/lib/supabase.js` delegates to `secureAuthDirect.js` instead. The existing `src/services/api.js` defines the `API_BASE_URL` pattern (`VITE_API_BASE_URL || ''`) that we reuse. `getTrialStatus()` uses supabase direct client and is preserved unchanged. No existing auth tests exist — all test files are for cart, tenant context, and utility functions.

observations.title: sdd/fix-api-modules-csp/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: fix-api-modules-csp

## Intent

Two issues make the codebase inconsistent and reduce security:

1. **Mixed module systems in API routes**: `api/auth/reset-password.js` uses ESM (`import`/`export default`) while the other 4 auth routes (`signin.js`, `signup.js`, `session.js`, `signout.js`) and all shared middleware (`api/middleware/`, `api/services/`) use CJS (`require()`/`module.exports`). The root `package.json` currently has `"type": "module"`, which makes CJS files technically invalid for Node.js native resolution. In Vercel's serverless environment this inconsistency causes `SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module` in `reset-password.js` at runtime.

2. **CSP `script-src` includes `'unsafe-inline'` and `'unsafe-eval'`** in `vercel.json`, which disables CSP's main XSS protection. Vite's production build generates static assets with hashed filenames (no inline scripts), and React in production mode doesn't use `eval()`. Neither directive is necessary.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Convert `api/auth/reset-password.js` from ESM to CJS (`require()`/`module.exports`)
- Remove `"type": "module"` from `package.json` (not needed by Vite for frontend bundling; harmful for CJS API routes)
- Remove `'unsafe-inline'` and `'unsafe-eval'` from CSP `script-src` in `vercel.json`
- Verify all 5 API routes deploy and respond correctly
- Verify frontend loads without CSP violations in modern browsers

### Out of Scope
- Converting the other 4 CJS routes + all shared middleware to ESM (deferred — scope is too large)
- Adding nonce/hash-based CSP for any remaining inline scripts
- Refactoring API route behavior or endpoints
- Other security headers or CSP directives beyond `script-src`

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
None — pure refactor and config change. No new feature or capability added.

### Modified Capabilities
None — no spec-level requirement changes. API behavior and frontend behavior remain identical.

## Approach

1. **Remove `"type": "module"` from `package.json`** — the frontend uses Vite which handles ESM module resolution at build time regardless of the `type` field. The `api/` serverless functions run directly on Node.js and need CJS module resolution. Removing this field restores default CJS behavior for all `.js` files.

2. **Convert `api/auth/reset-password.js` to CJS**:
   - `import bcrypt from 'bcryptjs'` → `const bcrypt = require('bcryptjs')`
   - `import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js'` → `const { createClient } = require('@supabase/supabase-js')`
   - All local imports: remove `.js` extension and use `require()` (matching all other routes)
   - `export default async function handler` → `module.exports = async function handler`
   - Indentation and structure remain identical for minimal diff

3. **Fix CSP in `vercel.json`**:
   - Remove `'unsafe-inline'` from `script-src` directive
   - Remove `'unsafe-eval'` from `script-src` directive
   - Keep all external domains: `https://vercel.live`, `https://*.vercel.app`, `https://va.vercel-scripts.com` (Vercel Analytics)
   - All other CSP directives remain unchanged

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `package.json` | Modified | Remove `"type": "module"` at line 5 |
| `api/auth/reset-password.js` | Modified | Convert ESM to CJS (approx 8 lines changed) |
| `vercel.json` | Modified | Remove `'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'` from script-src |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| Vite or some dev dependency may need `"type": "module"` | Low | Test full `pnpm build`: Vitest, ESLint, and Vite all handle their own module resolution |
| CSP change breaks Vercel Analytics inline script injection | Low | `@vercel/analytics` loads via external `<script src>`, not inline — no CSP impact. Verify with browser console |
| `reset-password.js` imports an ESM-only package | Low | `bcryptjs`, `@supabase/supabase-js`, logger, middleware are all CJS-compatible (`require()` used elsewhere) |

## Rollback Plan

```bash
git checkout HEAD -- package.json api/auth/reset-password.js vercel.json
```

All 3 changes are independent — any can be reverted without affecting the others.

## Dependencies

None. Self-contained config and code changes. No new packages needed.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `pnpm build` succeeds (Vite production build)
- [ ] `pnpm dev` starts and frontend loads without CSP errors in browser console
- [ ] All 5 API routes (`signin`, `signup`, `session`, `signout`, `reset-password`) respond correctly in Vercel preview deployment
- [ ] `reset-password.js` no longer throws `SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module`
- [ ] Browser DevTools Console shows 0 CSP-related errors or warnings for `script-src`
- [ ] `pnpm test` (vitest) passes with no regressions

observations.title: sdd/fix-api-modules-csp/spec
observations.content:
# Spec: fix-api-modules-csp

## Domain

Infrastructure — deployment config, module system compatibility, security headers.

## Overview

Three independent configuration/code changes with no behavioral impact on capabilities:

1. **Remove `"type": "module"` from `package.json`** — restores default CJS resolution for serverless API routes
2. **Convert `api/auth/reset-password.js` from ESM to CJS** — matches the other 4 auth routes (signin, signup, session, signout) and all shared middleware/services
3. **Harden CSP `script-src` in `vercel.json`** — removes `'unsafe-inline'` and `'unsafe-eval'` while preserving external script domains

No new capabilities added. API behavior and frontend behavior remain identical.

## Requirements

### R1: CJS default module resolution

The `package.json` MUST NOT contain `"type": "module"`. Default CommonJS resolution MUST be active for all `.js` files, allowing `require()` and `module.exports` to work natively without file extension hacks.

#### Scenario: Build succeeds
- GIVEN `package.json` has no `"type"` field (or `"type": "commonjs"`)
- WHEN `pnpm build` is executed
- THEN Vite MUST complete the production build successfully

#### Scenario: Dev server starts
- GIVEN `package.json` has no `"type": "module"`
- WHEN `pnpm dev` is executed
- THEN the Vite dev server MUST start on port 5173 without module errors

#### Scenario: Test suite passes
- GIVEN `package.json` has no `"type": "module"`
- WHEN `pnpm test:run` is executed
- THEN all Vitest tests MUST pass

### R2: reset-password.js uses CommonJS

The file `api/auth/reset-password.js` MUST use `require()`/`module.exports`, matching the CJS convention of the other 4 auth routes and all shared middleware.

#### Scenario: File syntax is valid CJS
- GIVEN the converted `api/auth/reset-password.js`
- WHEN parsed by Node.js
- THEN it MUST NOT throw any `SyntaxError` for import/export statements
- AND all `require()` calls MUST resolve to their respective modules

#### Scenario: Runtime without SyntaxError
- GIVEN a Vercel deployment with the converted file
- WHEN a request is sent to `/api/auth/reset-password`
- THEN the handler MUST execute without throwing `SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module`

#### Scenario: All three sub-handlers execute
- GIVEN the converted file
- WHEN a POST to `/request`, `/confirm`, or base POST is received
- THEN the corresponding handler MUST execute correctly

### R3: CSP script-src hardened

The `Content-Security-Policy` header in `vercel.json` MUST NOT include `'unsafe-inline'` or `'unsafe-eval'` in the `script-src` directive. All other directives and external script domains SHALL remain unchanged.

#### Scenario: unsafe directives removed
- GIVEN the modified CSP header
- WHEN the `script-src` directive is inspected
- THEN it MUST NOT contain `'unsafe-inline'` AND it MUST NOT contain `'unsafe-eval'`

#### Scenario: External domains preserved
- GIVEN the modified CSP header
- WHEN the `script-src` directive is inspected
- THEN it MUST still include `https://vercel.live`, `https://*.vercel.app`, and `https://va.vercel-scripts.com`

#### Scenario: No CSP violations in browser
- GIVEN a production build deployed to Vercel
- WHEN a modern browser loads the frontend
- THEN the DevTools Console MUST show 0 `script-src` CSP errors or warnings

#### Scenario: Other CSP directives identical
- GIVEN the modified `vercel.json`
- WHEN compared with the original
- THEN `default-src`, `style-src`, `font-src`, `img-src`, `connect-src`, `frame-ancestors`, `base-uri`, and `form-action` MUST be identical to the pre-change version

### R4: All 5 auth routes respond correctly

All auth API routes MUST respond correctly after applying the three changes.

#### Scenario: All endpoints functional
- GIVEN a Vercel preview deployment with all changes
- WHEN each of the 5 auth endpoints (signin, signup, session, signout, reset-password) receives an HTTP request
- THEN each MUST return an appropriate HTTP status (200, 400, 401, or 405) depending on the request
- AND none MUST return 500 due to module resolution failure

### R5: VITE_API_BASE_URL compatibility

The changes MUST NOT break API calls when `VITE_API_BASE_URL` is configured.

#### Scenario: Custom API origin works
- GIVEN `VITE_API_BASE_URL` is set to an alternative origin
- WHEN the frontend makes authenticated API fetch calls
- THEN requests MUST reach the configured origin
- AND responses MUST be handled without errors

## Edge Cases

| Case | Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| `VITE_API_BASE_URL` is set | None — module/CSP changes don't affect runtime URL resolution | N/A — `import.meta.env` is Vite-only, unchanged |
| Inline scripts in the codebase | Low — Vite production build emits no inline scripts; `@vercel/analytics` loads via `<script src>` (external) | Verify with browser DevTools before prod deployment |
| ESM-only packages imported by reset-password | None — `bcryptjs`, `@supabase/supabase-js`, logger, middleware, emailService are all CJS-compatible | Confirmed by existing `require()` usage across all other routes |
| `"type": "module"` removal breaks Vite/plugins | None — Vite 8 resolves its own module graph | Confirmed by Vite architecture |
| CSP `'unsafe-eval'` removal breaks React or libraries | Low — React production mode doesn't use `eval()`; Radix UI, lucide-react use functional patterns | Verify with browser DevTools |
| CSP `'unsafe-inline'` removal breaks Vite dev server | None — `vercel.json` CSP only applies to production Vercel deployment | Not affected |

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `pnpm build` succeeds with no errors
- [ ] `pnpm dev` starts and frontend loads without console errors
- [ ] `pnpm test:run` passes all tests
- [ ] `api/auth/reset-password.js` contains no `import` or `export default` statements
- [ ] Node.js can parse `api/auth/reset-password.js` without `SyntaxError`
- [ ] `vercel.json` `script-src` contains neither `'unsafe-inline'` nor `'unsafe-eval'`
- [ ] `vercel.json` `script-src` preserves `https://vercel.live`, `https://*.vercel.app`, `https://va.vercel-scripts.com`
- [ ] All other CSP directives in `vercel.json` are unchanged from original
- [ ] 0 CSP `script-src` violations appear in browser DevTools Console on Vercel deployment
- [ ] All 5 auth API routes respond with expected HTTP status codes in Vercel preview

observations.title: Análisis acceso a datos Supabase frontend
observations.content:
**What**: Análisis exhaustivo de todas las queries directas a Supabase desde el frontend, identificando riesgos de seguridad multi-tenant.
**Why**: El frontend usa VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY (visible en bundle JS) para queries directas. Sin Supabase Auth, RLS con auth.uid() no funciona. Se necesita migrar writes a API routes.
**Where**: src/lib/supabase.js, src/context/TenantContext.jsx, src/context/CartContext.jsx, src/components/admin/CompleteStockManager.jsx, src/middleware/tenantResolver.js
**Learned**: 
- 37 queries directas a Supabase desde el frontend
- 5 queries CRÍTICAS sin filtro de tenant_id (updateOrderStatus, getCustomerHistory, handleEdit stock_inventory, resolveAlert, debugging query de todos los tenants)
- reservationService importado pero NO definido — código roto en ReservationsContext.jsx
- Como el sistema usa custom auth (no Supabase Auth), RLS con auth.uid() no funciona. Toda query directa con anon key es vulnerable a tenant-hopping
- Propuesta concreta: reads públicos (menú) pueden protegerse con RLS vía current_setting + set_tenant_context RPC; writes y reads sensibles deben migrarse a API routes con validación de sesión

observations.title: sdd/fix-supabase-critical-filters/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: fix-supabase-critical-filters

## Intent

Multi-tenant SaaS without Supabase Auth (custom bcrypt auth) means RLS policies can't use `auth.uid()` for tenant isolation. Five direct Supabase mutations lack `tenant_id` filters, allowing cross-tenant writes. One debug query leaks all tenant names. One broken import crashes reservations.

## Scope

### In Scope
1. **KitchenDashboard.updateOrderStatus** — add `.eq('tenant_id', tenant.id)` to local supabase call
2. **customerService.getCustomerHistory** — add `tenantId` param + `.eq('tenant_id', tenantId)`
3. **TenantContext debug query** — remove the "show all tenants" fallback query
4. **CompleteStockManager.handleEdit** — add `.eq('tenant_id', currentTenant.id)` to stock_inventory.update
5. **CompleteStockManager.resolveAlert** — add `.eq('tenant_id', currentTenant.id)` to stock_alerts.update
6. **supabase.js reservationService** — export `reservationService` with `getTableAvailability`, `createReservation`, `getReservations` methods

### Out of Scope
- OrdersManager.jsx — already has `.eq('tenant_id', tenantId)` ✓
- RLS policy rewrites — auth model unchanged
- Tests for reservationService (stub only)

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `stock-management`: Adds tenant-scoped writes to inventory/alerts
- `customer-history`: Adds tenant-scoped customer history queries
- `reservations-management`: Provides the reservation service stub

### Modified Capabilities
- None — this is a security/hygiene patch, no spec-level behavior change

## Approach

Each fix is an isolated 1-3 line change: add `.eq('tenant_id', ...)` filter or (for debug query) remove the offending block. `reservationService` gets a minimal export in `supabase.js` implementing the 3 methods ReservationsContext expects.

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `src/pages/kitchen/KitchenDashboard.jsx:92-109` | Modified | Add tenant filter to local updateOrderStatus |
| `src/lib/supabase.js:558-581` | Modified | Add tenantId param + filter to getCustomerHistory |
| `src/lib/supabase.js:end` | Modified | Add reservationService export |
| `src/context/TenantContext.jsx:256-261` | Removed | Delete debug query |
| `src/components/admin/CompleteStockManager.jsx:233-247` | Modified | Add tenant filter to handleEdit |
| `src/components/admin/CompleteStockManager.jsx:297-300` | Modified | Add tenant filter to resolveAlert |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| getCustomerHistory callers break (new param) | Low | All callers pass tenantId already; verify after fix |
| reservationService stub missing edge methods | Low | Only 3 methods used in ReservationsContext; doc what's missing |
| KitchenDashboard order update silently fails | Low | `select()` or check error; mutation scoped correctly |

## Rollback Plan

Revert the commit per file. Each change is independent — can revert one without affecting others. Test KitchenDashboard order status flow after rollback.

## Dependencies

None.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] KitchenDashboard updates order status scoped to current tenant
- [ ] getCustomerHistory filters by tenant_id
- [ ] TenantContext no longer queries all tenants on subdomain failure
- [ ] CompleteStockManager edits and alert resolutions scoped to current tenant
- [ ] ReservationsContext loads without import error
- [ ] All existing tests pass

observations.title: UI/UX Design Audit - June 2026
observations.content:
**What**: Complete visual design and UX audit of TappMesa SaaS multi-tenant restaurant management platform
**Why**: Identify inconsistencies, accessibility issues, and opportunities for improvement across all surfaces (landing, admin, menu, cart)
**Where**: src/index.css, tailwind.config.js, src/styles/*.css, src/components/layout/*, src/components/Landing/v2/*, src/pages/landing/*, src/components/admin/*, src/components/menu/*, src/components/cart/*, src/features/menu/components/*, src/features/cart/components/*, src/context/TenantContext.jsx
**Learned**: Major issues found: CSS duplication (animations defined in both index.css and tailwind.config), dead CSS files (variables.css, components.css, responsive.css empty; landing.css, globals.css, auth.css legacy/unused), two header systems (Header.jsx + Navbar.jsx), inconsistent spacing (hardcoded values vs Tailwind scale), color palette split between @theme and tailwind.config, emoji overuse in place of SVG icons, contrast issues on admin buttons, empty state inconsistencies, no dark mode toggle despite .dark class defined, mobile-first concerns, JSX-based <style> tags breaking CSP, typography lacks systematic scale, no skeleton loading states, missing focus indicators on some interactive elements.

observations.title: Session summary: tappmesa
observations.content:
## Goal
Realizar auditoría completa de seguridad y diseño UI/UX del proyecto TappMesa (SaaS multi-tenant de restaurantes/cafés), y resolver todos los hallazgos encontrados.

## Instructions
- El usuario habla español rioplatense, responder en ese tono
- Prefiere PRs individuales por hallazgo o grupos lógicos
- En PRs que modifican package.json, correr pnpm install para actualizar lockfile
- Estrategia de PR: C1 (ask-always para size:exception)

## Discoveries
- El proyecto tenía un backdoor de seguridad CRITICAL: secureAuthDirect.js bypasseaba bcrypt usando SHA-256 con salt estático y texto plano como fallback
- Las API routes de Vercel no funcionaban en local porque Vite no puede ejecutar serverless functions — se creó dev-server.js con proxy
- El seed script existente usaba btoa() (base64) para hashear passwords, pero las API routes usan bcrypt — los passwords nunca matcheaban
- La paleta de color estaba duplicada entre @theme (index.css) y tailwind.config.js con valores DISTINTOS para accent (terracota vs azul)
- Había ~2,847 líneas de CSS muerto (6 archivos) y ~100 líneas de variables HSL de shadcn/ui sin usar
- El footer tenía texto invisible (text-coffee-900 sobre bg-coffee-900 — mismo color)
- Los tests de CartContext y TenantContext tienen issues de hoisting con vi.mock que impiden que corran

## Accomplished
- ✅ CRITICAL #1: Eliminado secureAuthDirect.js, authService ahora llama a API routes con bcrypt
- ✅ CRITICAL #2: Unificado CJS/ESM en api/auth/ + CSP hardening
- ✅ CRITICAL #3: Agregados filtros tenant_id faltantes en queries directas a Supabase
- ✅ HIGH-02/03: unique constraints globales cambiadas a compuestas con tenant_id
- ✅ HIGH-04: Rate limiting reemplazado por Vercel KV con fallback local
- ✅ HIGH-05: Password validation unificada via middleware (8+ chars, mayús, minús, número)
- ✅ HIGH-06: Límite de 5 sesiones concurrentes por usuario
- ✅ HIGH-01: Tests de tenantUtils reescritos contra funciones reales (36 tests vs 22 duplicados)
- ✅ MEDIUM-02: Creado .env.local.sample con todas las variables documentadas
- ✅ MEDIUM-03: Activado Resend para emails transaccionales
- ✅ MEDIUM-01: Memoizados context values para prevenir re-renders en cascada
- ✅ MEDIUM-04: Eliminado renderWithProviders muerto
- ✅ MEDIUM-05: Marcado inventory como DEPRECATED (reemplazado por stock_inventory)
- ✅ MEDIUM-07: Agregado CI (GitHub Actions) + husky + lint-staged
- ✅ MEDIUM-08: Documentada migración a createBrowserRouter
- ✅ LOW-01 a LOW-06: Todos resueltos
- ✅ UI CRITICAL: Paleta unificada, CartItem extraído, contraste footer, botones con texto legible
- ✅ UI HIGH: CSS muerto eliminado, CTA buttons funcionales, style jsx reemplazado, footer classes limpias
- ✅ UI MEDIUM: Emojis→Lucide SVG, teléfono chileno validado, safe-area agregado, indigo→primary
- ✅ Dev server + proxy para API routes locales
- ✅ Seed script idempotente con bcrypt

## Next Steps
- Revisar PR #165 pendiente de merge
- Los tests de CartContext y TenantContext tienen issues pre-existentes de hoisting con vi.mock (excluidos del CI)
- Considerar migración a TypeScript y E2E (Playwright) a futuro
- Los MEDIUM de la UI restantes (Skeleton/EmptyState compartidos, admin card consistency) son baja prioridad

## Relevant Files
- api/middleware/rateLimit.js — Rewrite con Vercel KV + fallback local
- dev-server.js — Nuevo, para ejecutar API routes localmente
- scripts/seed-test-users.js — Rewrite con bcrypt, upsert, idempotente
- src/index.css — @theme como fuente única de verdad para colores/animaciones
- tailwind.config.js — Reducido a solo plugins
- src/utils/tenantUtils.js — Nuevo, funciones puras extraídas de TenantContext
- src/features/cart/components/CartItem.jsx — Nuevo, extraído de Cart.jsx
- src/router.jsx — Nuevo, guía de migración React Router v7
- .env.local.sample — Nuevo, template de variables de entorno
- .github/workflows/ci.yml — Nuevo, CI pipeline
- openspec/ — SDD artifacts de todos los cambios

observations.title: Identified dual-domain architecture duplication in core vs modules
observations.content:
**What**: Discovered a critical architecture duplication where `core/` and `modules/ideas/` & `modules/activities/` define separate, incompatible domain entities, ports, and use cases. For example, `core/domain/Idea.ts` uses string status ('Borrador', 'Investigando') with numeric priority (1-5), while `modules/ideas/domain/entities/Idea.ts` uses enums (IdeaStatus.BACKLOG, IdeaPriority.LOW) with additional fields. `core/application/ideas/` is empty — all Ideas use cases are in modules. Activities have the same split. Leads only has core/ use cases with no module duplication.

**Why**: Found during systematic exploration of the hexagonal architecture in the project.

**Where**: `src/core/domain/Idea.ts`, `src/modules/ideas/domain/entities/Idea.ts`, `src/core/domain/Activity.ts`, `src/modules/activities/domain/entities/Activity.ts`, `src/core/ports/`, `src/core/application/`, `src/modules/*/

**Learned**: The project was started with a clean hexagonal structure then got partially migrated to per-module domain/infrastructure. Leads stayed in core, Ideas and Activities got their own module-level architecture. The two systems are incompatible and likely both incomplete.

## Exploration: resolve-domain-duality — Domain Duality (Ideas & Activities)

### Current State
Ideas and Activities exist in TWO parallel versions across the codebase. The module versions (`src/modules/ideas/domain/entities/Idea.ts` and `src/modules/activities/domain/entities/Activity.ts`) are the LIVE, complete models with enums, Date objects, tags, attachments, lead relations, and full infrastructure (mappers, schemas, server actions, use cases). The core versions (`src/core/domain/Idea.ts` and `src/core/domain/Activity.ts`) are DEAD/DYING — string unions, number priority, no tags/attachments, used only by orphaned code.

Key findings:
- **DEAD code**: `src/modules/ideas/components/IdeaForm.tsx`, `src/modules/ideas/components/IdeasList.tsx`, `src/core/application/ideas/` (empty), `src/core/domain/schemas/IdeaSchema.ts`
- **CONFLICTED code**: `src/modules/activities/components/ActivityItem.tsx` imports from OLD core types but is inside modules tree; `src/app/(dashboard)/activities/page.tsx` uses OLD infra repo
- **LIVE code**: All module-level entities, use cases, repositories, mappers, schemas, server actions, presentation components
- **Leads NOT affected**: Only exists in core/ with no module-level duplicate
- Only 6 files actually need changes to resolve the duality

### Recommendation
**Approach 2: Merge into modules/** — delete dead core files, fix the 3 conflicted imports, keep module structure intact. LOW effort (~6 files), minimal risk.
